commit_reviews.summary: Cross-cutting additions (history endpoint, rate limiting, TTL cleanup) that follow the existing HTTP-handler and Redis-with-fallback patterns, but block the event loop with synchronous SQLite deletes and send rate-limit errors typed as "system" while its own test asserts "error".

compounding_issues: Binary build artifacts committed to git from Session 1 onward (__pycache__/*.pyc) and re-committed on every change; Session 5 also commits messages.db
asyncio.sleep(0.01) timing hack added to process_request in Session 3 ("let a just-received WebSocket frame finish") is baked into production code to appease tests and carried through Sessions 4-5
Seed codebase (Flask Auth API) was wholly discarded in Session 1's greenfield rewrite, so no seed structure carried forward
Subscription state is duplicated across the Redis set and the local ClientRegistry; delivery filtering relies only on the local registry, so the two can drift
Session 4's refactor silently dropped per-client dead-connection removal in broadcast (previously tracked via gather result inspection)
key_decisions: Session 1: total rewrite to an asyncio/websockets architecture, discarding the Flask seed entirely
Session 1: thread-safe ClientRegistry abstraction as the shared state backbone for the server
Session 3: optional Redis pub/sub with graceful local-delivery fallback, keeping the system runnable and testable without Redis
Session 3: SQLite MessageStore isolated behind its own thread + RLock, kept separate from the asyncio event loop
Session 4: BaseTransport ABC extracting WebSocket handling behind a pluggable transport contract, with API and tests kept identical
Session 5: dual-mode rate limiter (Redis counters primary, in-memory fallback) reusing the Session 3 graceful-degradation pattern
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically. Session 1 produced a small, clean greenfield core (~174 LOC) with passing broadcast/disconnect tests; Session 2 added channel subscriptions and REST channel endpoints with new tests; Session 3 layered Redis pub/sub and SQLite persistence behind a resilient optional-broker design; Session 4 was a disciplined refactor that extracted a BaseTransport abstraction while keeping the public API and all tests byte-for-byte unchanged; Session 5 added rate limiting, /history pagination, and a TTL cleanup task on top of the refactored layer, ending at 569 LOC with all 11 tests passing. The only downward drift was hygiene-related (committed .pyc binaries, a sleep-based timing hack), while the architecture grew steadily more modular and abstract.
story_review.summary: A near-textbook coherent five-session arc — greenfield core, feature addition, integration, refactor, cross-cutting — where each session built directly on the prior one and finished with a transport-abstracted, fully tested notification service.
